items.body_excerpt:
Presented By
NRL Late Mail: Round 24 - Teddy ruled out; Knights stars return
The Roosters have been dealt a blow ahead of Thursday's top-of-the-table clash with the Panthers with James Tedesco succumbing to an ankle injury.
The fullback was initially named to return at CommBank Stadium but dropped out in the 24-hour team update. Cody Ramsey will line up at fullback in his place.
Some positive news for Panthers coach Ivan Cleary, who is juggling an injured fullback and an expectant father in the lead-up to Thursday's match.
Fullback Dylan Edwards has missed three games with a shoulder injury and remains in the extended squad after Wednesday's 24-hour update.
"He’s a chance. We’ll see how he goes today but he’s definitely a chance," Cleary told media on Wednesday.
Five-eighth Jack Cogger stayed in Sydney last week for the birth of his child but the wait continues for he and his wife so Cleary has Jack Cole on standby.
"We've got contingency plans, sometimes some things are more important than footy," Cleary said.

NRL Casualty Ward: Fresh Reynolds injury; Roosters' Teddy blow
Broncos veteran Adam Reynolds faces a battle to return to the field before hanging up the boots after suffering a calf strain at training on Wednesday.
The premiership winner has not played since suffering a head knock in the Round 22 loss to the Knights and the latest setback puts his hopes of playing out his final season before retiring at the end of the year at risk.
In a statement, the Broncos said Reynolds will be assessed on a weekly basis to determine a return to play.
"Scans at the Clive Berghofer Centre’s Qscan facility confirmed that Broncos captain Adam Reynolds sustained a grade 1 soleus strain on his right calf at training yesterday," the club said.
"His return-to-play timeline will be determined on a week-by-week basis."
Gun fullback James Tedesco has fallen short in his bid to return from ankle injury for Thursday's top-of-the-table showdown between the Roosters and Panthers.
The Rooster was named to return after missing last week's win over the Bulldogs but was ruled out of the CommBank Stadium clash on Wednesday night.
Rival fullback Dylan Edwards is still a chance of lining up in the match as he looks to play his first game since Round 20 due to a shoulder injury. The Penrith star remains in the extended squad after the 24-hour update.
The Panthers will be missing captain Isaah Yeo due to a pectoral injury suffered in last week's loss to the Warriors.
The NSW and Australian skipper received some positive news on Monday, with scans revealing he does not need season-ending surgery and could return at the start of the finals series.
While the Roosters expect Tedesco to return on Thursday night, they remain without representative stars Angus Crichton (foot) and Daniel Tupou (shoulder).
In an update at his weekly press conference, coach Trent Robinson said he hopes the pair will be back before the end of the regular season.
"They’re a few weeks away still," Robinson said. "Toups is back running well, with his shoulder injury so that’s still a few weeks away.
"Gussie had a medical appointment on Monday. There’s some good progression there and he’s starting to get back into some more movement. Again, it’s not within the next week or two but it’d be nice [to have him back] before the end of the regular season as well."
There's mixed news for the Rabbitohs ahead of their crucial clash with the Bulldogs, with winger Campbell Graham named to return from a calf injury.
The Australian representative was a late withdrawal from last week's win over the Eels.
In less positive news, South Sydney will be without halfback Ashton Ward for the remainder of the season after he suffered a high-grade hamstring tear while kicking in last week's win over Parramatta.

Penrith winger Tom Jenkins is set to dig deep into a bag of tricks developed as a state high jumper as he looks to outgun Roosters star Mark Nawaqanitawase on Thursday night.
The two players will go head-to-head at CommBank Stadium in one of many fascinating positional battles in the top-of-the-table clash.
Nawaqanitawase has developed into one of the biggest aerial threats in the game and has produced a string of freakish players throughout the past two seasons.

Jenkins is no slouch in the air himself, with nine of his 28 tries this year coming from bombs and cross-field kicks, but he will be at a height disadvantage on Thursday night.
That’s where the Panther’s background as a high jumper comes in, with Jenkins to lean on some of those skills in his contest with Nawaqanitawase.
“He’s such a special talent,” Jenkins said. “He’s one of those people who’s a massive aerial threat and I’m excited to go up against him. He’s a quality player and it will be sad to see him leave the NRL at the end of this year because I enjoy watching him.
“I was a high jumper when I was younger so that puts me in good stead for [catching bombs]. I’ve done a lot of training and put a lot of work into it, being good in the air brings a different aspect to my game.”

Ready to roar: Dramatic week driving Panthers towards Roosters showdown
The Penrith Panthers are determined to let their football do the talking as they navigate a dramatic lead-in to Thursday's top-of-the-table showdown with the Roosters.
It's been a challenging week on and off the field for Ivan Cleary's men, with captain Isaah Yeo injuring his pectoral in last Friday's loss to the Warriors.
The positive news that Yeo has avoided season-ending surgery and could return in time for the finals was quickly overshadowed by the announcement that Brian To'o will depart at the end of next year to join the PNG Chiefs.
Brian on the double
The situation threatens to distract from Penrith's quest for the minor premiership, with the winner of Thursday's match at CommBank Stadium to take sole ownership of first place with three rounds remaining in the season.
The Panthers, however, have dealt with player departures and late-season injuries on a yearly basis since their run of success commenced in 2020 and prop Liam Henry said they are well-positioned to put the drama aside before the Roosters clash.
"There's always going to be off-field distractions," Henry said. "The club does a wonderful job with the players to get them to focus on what's important.
"We don't pay too much attention to what happens outside these four walls.
"We've taken some great lessons out of last week's game. The Roosters have been going well, they've got a great side and a good forward pack so we're looking forward to Thursday night."

The Iceman with a crucial 40/20
Winger Tom Jenkins is among the cohort to have extended beyond 2027 and he's hopeful as many teammates as possible remain with the club when Peter Wallace takes over in 2028.
"They all have faith and trust in Wall that he's going to lead us to success," Jenkins said. "Everyone in this building has full confidence. I'm not too sure about the boys' contracts and how that influences them but it wouldn't be in a negative way.
"As somebody who's re-signed long term, I'd love to see those boys follow suit, I'd love to see everyone stay. The sad thing about footy is it's a business and when you're going well, other teams want your players. That's part of it but hopefully the boys re-sign."
To'o's decision to depart the club at the end of next season drew mixed emotions within Panthers HQ, with players both surprised at the move and excited to see their teammate embark on a new challenge at an expansion club.

"It was a bit of a surprise but in the same sense, it's footy," Jenkins said. "I'm stoked for him that he can do this for his family and he's deserving of whatever comes next.
"For him, the next chapter is PNG but that's in 2028. He's got a massive job here, which he'll play a big role in our 2027 season and the rest of this season."

The Roosters have set their sights on their first minor premiership in eight years as they look to unseat the Panthers at the top of the table.
The two teams are level on 36 points heading into a Thursday-night showdown at CommBank Stadium, with the winner to claim pole position in the run to the finals.
The Roosters have closed the gap with the Panthers throughout the past month and drew level with a scratchy victory over the Bulldogs last Friday night just a couple of hours after Penrith fell to the Warriors in Auckland.
Smith steps up
This season looms as the Roosters' best chance to win the premiership since their last title in 2019 and they're eager to climb to first on the ladder with a win on Thursday night.
"To finish first at the end of the regular season is a cool achievement," winger Billy Smith said. "That's our most important thing at the moment.
"We're happy but we're definitely not content with where we're at. We're still chasing our best and we were a long way from home [last week]. It's good we're still winning games and not playing our best footy so we've got a lot of room to improve.
"We're going to have to be on our best against Penrith because we're pretty clear on where we want to get to this year."

Remarkably, at least one team from each of the nine previous matches has gone on to play in the grand final, with three sides lifting the trophy at the end of the year.
The last late-season top-of-the-table clash occurred two years ago, when the competition-leading Storm travelled to Penrith and came away with a two-point win in a game best remembered for Nathan Cleary's shoulder injury.
The Panthers bounced back to defeat Melbourne in the decider a couple of months later.
After a slight hiccup last year, Penrith have set the standard this season and have sat on top of the ladder since Round 4.
The Roosters, in contrast, have managed to fly under the radar despite boasting one of the most star-studded rosters in the competition.
Trent Robinson's side has hovered between third and sixth for much of the season before climbing into second a fortnight ago.
Perhaps the scariest part of the Roosters rise is the fact they sit equal first despite some wild swings in form this year.
The players were disappointed with their performance in last week's win over the Bulldogs but Spencer Leniu said Thursday's match is a chance to make a statement against the competition favourites.

"They're a well-oiled machine and they've been the benchmark for the competition the last couple of years," Leniu said.
"Playing the Bulldogs will put us in good stead, they play a similar style and it's a preview of what we're going to come up against this week. They're our biggest competition and this week we'll see what this team's about."
The Roosters are set to receive a major boost with fullback James Tedesco likely to return on Thursday night.

August 13 th 2026, 12:53pm , By: Ben Bridge
Friday Night Football at 4 Pines Park shapes as a genuine ‘win or go home’ game for Manly, although at this stage it may already be too late to save their season. The Sea Eagles have lost five consecutive matches, fallen from third to 10th on the ladder and now return from a trip to Perth where they blew a 14-0 lead before being hammered 42-20 by Melbourne. Despite finally getting back to Brookvale, Manly arguably have the worse travel setup against a Dolphins side coming off a Brisbane derby and now officially assured of playing finals football.
The market is basically where I have this game rated, so this is not a major edge. However, the alternative margin appeals more than forcing the traditional spread. The Dolphins have secured their first finals berth and can now attack the final month without the same pressure that has followed them in previous late season collapses. If the shackles come off, this backline can put a number on a Manly side whose defensive confidence looks completely shot.
Tom Trbojevic remains unavailable with his hamstring injury, leaving Clayton Faulalo at fullback. The Dolphins are close to full strength through their spine and backline, with Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow, Isaiya Katoa, Herbie Farnworth, Jack Bostock, Selwyn Cobbo and Jamayne Isaako all named.
Sea Eagles vs Dolphins Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Round 24
Sea Eagles’ Season Falling Apart
Manly’s 42-20 loss to Melbourne in Perth might have been the performance that finally broke their finals campaign. The opening stages were actually excellent. The Sea Eagles raced to a 14-0 advantage and looked capable of snapping their losing run, only for the Storm to score 42 unanswered points as Manly completely lost control of the contest. Taniela Paseka also suffered a suspected MCL injury, adding another setback to a side already without Turbo.
That second half collapse is the greater concern than the raw result. Manly’s attack still has weapons. Jason Saab, Tolu Koula, Reuben Garrick, Lehi Hopoate and Haumole Olakau’atu can all generate points, while Jamal Fogarty provides a reliable kicking game. The issue is what happens when momentum shifts against them. Over the past month, Manly have been beaten by Parramatta, Gold Coast and North Queensland before the Melbourne loss, surrendering leads, and falling apart defensively with alarming regularity.
Kieran Foran has been forced into further changes this week. Faulalo returns at fullback, but Manly are still without Trbojevic and have lost Paseka from the middle. Four weeks of the regular 2026 NRL season to go and the race for the minor premiership, Top 4 and Top 8 spots is going into overdrive.
NRL Round 24 kicks off with a top-of-the-table clash, while six of the remaining seven encounters are between teams inside the Top 8 and opponents in the bottom half – with the Souths-Canterbury showdown on Saturday shaping as being particularly pivotal.
Read on for our complete NRL Round 24 predictions, preview and best bets to place on the footy this weekend!
NRL
CommBank Stadium • Thursday 13th Aug
The minor premiership could be decided in this 1 v 2 showdown at CommBank Stadium.
FORM: The Panthers have now lost four of their last seven, following up a big win over Canberra with a convincing 28-12 defeat to the Warriors.
The Roosters have won eight straight, coming from 10 points down to see off the Bulldogs 20-18 last Friday.
INS AND OUTS: Lindsay Smith moves to lock, and Liam Henry comes in at prop with Isaah Yeo sidelined for Penrith. Jack Cogger lines up at five-eighth after being a late scratching last week, while Dylan Edwards has been named in the reserves. James Tedesco returns for the Roosters.
KEY MATCH-UP: It’s an Origin rematch as Nathan Cleary squares off against Sam Walker.
HISTORY: The Panthers have won 12 of their last 13 against the Roosters, including a 40-4 rout in Round 3 this season.
KEY STAT: The Panthers have scored 30-plus points in eight of their last 11 games against the Roosters.
VERDICT: The favourites to meet in the grand final in seven weeks’ time, there’s plenty at stake with the winner likely to take out the minor premiership and the loser potentially facing a qualifying final trip to Auckland.
The Panthers have had a rough run and will be smarting from getting ambushed by the Warriors, but there’s arguably more pressure on the Roosters to buck the trend of horrendous results against the era’s preeminent team.
The Roosters remain unproven in heavyweight duels – though last week was a step in the right direction – and the Panthers look good value as a very narrow favourite.
Prediction: Back the Panthers to Win @ $1.77

4 Pines Park • Friday 14th Aug
The Sea Eagles are spiralling ahead of this must-win home assignment against the fifth-placed Dolphins.
FORM: Manly has lost five straight, conceding 128 points in their last three games against the Titans, Sharks and Storm.
The Dolphins have won three in a row, albeit somewhat patchily in the past fortnight against the Dragons (28-22) and Broncos (40-32) – trailing 24-0 in the latter.
INS AND OUTS: Clayton Faulalo returns at fullback for Manly with Lehi Hopoate shifting to the wing and Blake Wilson dropping out. Taniela Paseka (knee) is out, so Nathan Brown starts at prop.
The Dolphins have lost Kurt Donoghoe to a thumb injury, but Ray Stone and Jake Averillo are back on the bench.
KEY MATCH-UP: Blues teammates Jack Bostock and Tolu Koula are set for an absorbing centre duel.
HISTORY: The Dolphins are 1-3 against the Sea Eagles and will have terrifying memories of their most recent meeting, when Manly powered to a 52-18 win in Redcliffe in Kieran Foran’s first match as interim coach.
KEY STAT: These clubs’ four encounters all produced at least 54 points, with three of them seeing 70-plus points scored.
VERDICT: Manly’s finals bid has completely unravelled under a heavy injury toll as interim-turned-fulltime coach Kieran Foran searches for answers. Their drop-off in defensive resolve has been the most alarming feature of their losing streak.
The Dolphins have all but sealed their maiden finals appearance, but they’ll be looking for a complete performance after struggling to put away a couple of also-rans in the past two weeks. Near enough to full-strength, however, the visitors’ firepower should have a tackle-shy Sea Eagles outfit very nervous.
